Output-error ellipses prefer a different lattice point

Output-error ellipses prefer a different lattice point Illustrative mechanism · not full AWQ/GPTQ Previous Next Reset Illustrative mechanism · not full AWQ/GPTQ. Fixed unit grid; only row 0 and two active features. Contours are output SSE, not weight distance. Arrows illustrate sequential compensation, not a global lattice-search algorithm. The conceptual route fixes the first coordinate to zero, compensates the second to .645, then rounds to one. Gram [[1,1],[1,2]] is an uncentered feature cross-product, not Pearson correlation; the second feature is constant, so its Pearson coefficient is undefined. Ellipses use SSE on both samples; a circle would instead measure isotropic weight error. The grid extends only locally; real codes span −7…7.

Slide L03

GPTQ: choose the compensation from inputs

GPTQ: choose the compensation from inputs Worked CPU arithmetic · not model measurements $$a=\frac{(.49-0)\sum_n X_{n0}X_{n1}}{\sum_n X_{n1}^{2}}=\frac{.49}{2}=.245$$ a weight correction Adjust the unrounded second weight n 2 calibration samples Cross-product 1; energy 2 .40 + .245 = .645 → round to 1. Final codes: [0,1]. Minimizes (−.49 + a)² + a² before the next rounding. GPTQ §§3–4 . This one-remaining-coordinate least-squares update explains compensation. Full GPTQ uses inverse-Hessian information, damping, Cholesky and blocks. Those implementation details are optional; the mechanism is mandatory.

vLLM service

Slide L04

Serving hatch

One kitchen; two sides of the hatch. The client sees an HTTP contract. Behind it, tokenization, scheduling, model workers and GPU kernels form the service. The hatch separates API behavior from engine behavior. Avoid claiming that the illustration shows vLLM's exact process topology.

The demo works. The SDK request fails.

Two independent planes: identity/chat-template contract and transport/proxy behavior. Ask which endpoint to probe first.

The map is a debugging order, not a claim of exact process count.

Control plane and token data are not the same

Control plane and token data are not the same Trace discipline Control Load revision, set served name and limits, accept/cancel a request, report readiness and errors. Data Render message text, tokenize, run prefill/decode, emit token deltas and account for usage. This separation helps identify why a 404 or 400 can occur without any GPU work.

Engine Admission and queue state decide when the GPU sees work. Worker Weights, KV state and kernels produce logits; failures include OOM and unsupported paths. Walk through a wrong-model 404: stop at API. Then an OOM: trace to worker/admission. The diagram is a role map, not a process tree.

Active slots do not remove queueing

Do not solve it by deleting the model cache; that affects startup and does not change live GPU capacity.

Slide L04

Request logs can contain sensitive prompts

Request logs can contain sensitive prompts Data hygiene LOGGING Record metadata, not raw user text by default Request ID, model revision, token counts, status and phase times usually support triage. If raw prompts are ever logged, control access, retention and redaction explicitly. The lab uses synthetic prompts but still treats its server log as local evidence, not an automatic public artifact.

Slide L04

Failure: every clean launch downloads weights again

Failure: every clean launch downloads weights again Production scenario D Detect Startup duration scales with network transfer; logs show repeated fetch/resolve. A failed download looks like a model failure even though GPU is idle. Mitigate Prefetch one immutable revision, keep the model cache across runs, start from the local snapshot and fail offline if expected files are missing. This directly addresses the course's earlier repeated clean-run downloads. Do not commit multi-GB model files into Git as a shortcut.

Slide L04

Use a bounded readiness window

Use a bounded readiness window Operational phase FAIL CLOSED Process exit or deadline → incident, not infinite wait The lab allows five minutes for its small local service. The judge has a separate 45-minute startup policy for immutable student submissions. Neither timeout is a performance score by itself. Do not transfer the lab deadline to the judge or vice versa. The bounds serve different workflows.

Slide L04

Capture versions with the result

Capture versions with the result Provenance Layer Record artifact model + tokenizer immutable revision runtime vLLM, Python, PyTorch, CUDA, driver device GPU name, memory, compute capability launch flags, cache path, served name Do not include secrets in launch-argument evidence. Record a redacted command or structured fields.

Slide L04

Teardown has observable acceptance checks

Teardown has observable acceptance checks One server process tree Check Pass evidence Failure action owned server process tree has exited bounded terminate, then escalate loopback port no listener on owned port identify owner before restarting GPU state baseline restored stop the next GPU task immutable snapshot still cached and verified reuse offline next week Stopping the parent alone may leave workers. Verify the actual process tree and resource baseline. Never kill unrelated user processes. Keep snapshots, discard only owned disposable process state.

Slide L04

One smoke request is not a load result

One smoke request is not a load result Scope warning Readiness “Chat works, therefore this instance supports 64 clients.” Reveal the missing test A smoke request proves one path and one state. Load testing needs a defined concurrency, prompt/output distribution, successful-output goodput, p95 latency and error accounting. Topic 06 supplies the controlled concurrency experiment. Do not overload this introductory service lab.

Slide L04

What survives a clean restart?

What survives a clean restart? Pause · state inventory STATE Server process · model cache · result evidence Which state should be deleted, which reused, and which sanitized before sharing? Explain why a clean service process need not imply a clean model download. Delete/stop process state; retain immutable cache; preserve sanitized evidence. Never persist private keys or hidden judge inputs.

Slide L04

Prove service

07 / 07 Prove it A launch command plus client evidence becomes a service contract. Collect positive and negative tests; an unrun GPU notebook remains unverified evidence.

Slide L04

Lab: small pinned model, one bounded process

Lab: small pinned model, one bounded process Startup + API smoke SEMINAR Qwen2.5-0.5B · vLLM 0.29 · localhost Prefetch the immutable snapshot once, launch with a 2048-token context cap, four active sequences and 45% GPU-memory target. Wait for /v1/models with a five-minute deadline. The flags intentionally bound the lab. GPU compatibility and package installation still need a real runtime; no benchmark is claimed from structural validation.

Slide L04

CPU parsing and GPU smoke prove different things

CPU parsing and GPU smoke prove different things Lab entry points Path Runs without GPU? Evidence synthetic byte replay yes, standard library UTF8/SSE/client states recorded transcript replay yes reinspection of one old run fresh vLLM server smoke no, CUDA required this deployment works now concurrency benchmark separate later topic load distribution and failures Students arrange a CUDA GPU. CPU checks are useful immediately but cannot stand in for the fresh service smoke. Keep all model assets cached. The new replay and historical smoke stay labeled separately.

Trace a client-visible service, not an open port

Trace a client-visible service, not an open port Pinned Topic 04 · step with → 01 Identity /v1/models advertises topic04 ; wrong name returns 404 frontend 02 Ordinary chat content + finish_reason=stop in one 0.748 s request complete 03 Raw stream 11 JSON frames and terminal [DONE] terminal 04 Context guard 2,329 rendered tokens &gt; 2,048 cap → HTTP 400 reject 05 Clean stop terminate the one service; confirm port and GPU return to baseline release Single-client API smoke · sanitized evidence ; no load or p95 claim. Slide L04

Keep the implementation contract versioned

Keep the implementation contract versioned Primary reading vLLM · serve CLI reference vLLM · online serving route and parameter support vLLM · engine arguments and memory/context limits OpenAI Python SDK · client and streaming behavior Kwon et al. · PagedAttention paper Documentation moves between releases. Students must report their installed versions and check the corresponding flags and routes.

Slide L04

What proves your server is ready for this client?

What proves your server is ready for this client? Exit ticket THREE PROOFS Identity · complete stream · expected failure Name the exact model string, the terminal signal that makes a stream complete, and one negative request that should fail without GPU work. The answer is not “the port is open.” Ask for /v1/models , chat/SSE, and a controlled error.

Slide L04

Service contract plate

Tickets in, complete plates out. The service contract includes identity, limits, completion, errors and a recoverable lifecycle—not just generated text. Return to the opening incident. The client-visible boundary is now explicit and testable.

Slide L04

Next scheduler

Now inspect the scheduler. Topic 05 derives PagedAttention and continuous batching: how live requests share KV memory and GPU iterations after the API admits them. The next topic explains the engine's internal memory and scheduling mechanisms; do not pretend this smoke lab measured their high-load behavior.
